cases.place_destination: Constitución (multiple districts: Cerro Centinella, Quinta Gaete y Villa Los Verdes), and outside

year_start.evidence: En diciembre del año 2010 se firmó un convenio entre la empresa Arauco, constructoras y SERVIU Maule a objeto de ejecutar cinco proyectos habitacionales en Constitución para 1.390 familias beneficiadas con el subsidio de vivienda.

households.evidence: [para] Sources give 1,390 subsidy families for the five city-wide Arauco-SERVIU projects and 50 'tsunami resistant' houses in La Poza, but no count of La Poza households relocated.

trigger.evidence: el tejido social quedó fracturado, tras la relocalización, especialmente de los habitantes del sector La Poza (after the 27F 2010 earthquake and tsunami)

lead.evidence: una alianza pública-privada para la reconstrucción integrada por el municipio de la ciudad, el Ministerio de Vivienda y Urbanismo (MINVU) y la empresa Arauco y, con el apoyo de la oficina de arquitectura Elemental; [para] citizen participation was not binding except in isolated cases.

single_owner.evidence: [para] Planning by a public-private alliance (municipality, MINVU, Arauco, Elemental); housing executed through a convenio between Arauco, construction firms and SERVIU Maule.

resident_site_choice.evidence: [para] Families were relocated outside the urban area on the argument that no land was available in the tsunami risk zone; participation was non-binding.

tenure_destination.evidence: Sources mention 'subsidio de vivienda' but do not describe tenure at the destination.

hazard_binding.evidence: Sources mention tsunami inundation levels (SHOA) for the risk zone but not how destination sites were screened.

funding.evidence: [para] State housing subsidies plus Arauco participation; the funding instrument is not specified.

distance.evidence: [para] Destinations are districts of Constitución (Cerro Centinela, Quinta Gaete, Villa Los Verdes) described as peripheral / outside the urban area; no distance given.

hazard_at_destination.evidence: No hazard at the destination sites reported.

livelihoods.evidence: Fisher families are mentioned, but livelihood outcomes at the destination are not described.

overall.evidence: Los entrevistados, ya sean residentes como agentes públicos y privados califican la reconstrucción con una nota 4,2 en el caso de Constitución (Chilean 1-7 scale); the paper frames it as 'Reconstrucción exclusionaria'.

cases.notes: Both papers look at reconstruction in Constitución as a whole. La Poza details are thin. The 4.2 rating covers the whole Constitución reconstruction, not only the La Poza relocation. INVI also says two coastal plots went to relocating former La Poza residents: 'Dos predios en torno al borde costero fueron destinados para la relocalización de los antiguos residentes de La Poza'.

trigger.evidence: [para] Nagua communities face sea-related climate risks, but the source does not say whether the move followed a specific event.

distance.evidence: [para] Houses were moved 'fuera del área de trabajo'; no distance given.

livelihoods.evidence: El caso más notorio son los pescadores de La Playa, cuyas viviendas fueron reubicadas fuera del área de trabajo, con lo cual, según los mismos, se redujo la capacidad de hacer negocio.

overall.evidence: [para] The source gives no overall judgement beyond noting that relocation is not always accepted because it breaks traditional livelihoods.

cases.notes: Del Rosario et al. (2012, IDIAF) mention the case in one passage. La Playa is a rural section of Nagua municipality, 3.5 km from the municipal seat (Tabla 2). I did not find 'Matancita' in the extracted text; the match comes from the sample frame.

year_start.evidence: [para] CU survey report Table 2 (move-in year by site): St. Francis (= Suribao) 82.3% of respondents moved in 2017, 17.7% in 2018.

households.evidence: Suribao NHA 1000 300 73 (Table 1: planned occupancy, validated occupancy Oct. 2017, sample size)

trigger.evidence: Following Typhoon Haiyan, the city government decided to relocate informal settlers (up to 40 percent of the city's population) to the largely undeveloped northern edges of the city

lead.evidence: Suribao is listed as an NHA project. 'Notably, none of the case communities included community members in decision-making, such as where to develop the relocation site.'

single_owner.evidence: The NHA built the site ('they [the NHA] have railroaded everything. They did not get the necessary development permits beforehand'). Water sat with the city: 'The city stalled relocation transfers to completed houses in 2016 because of severely limited capacity to provide water via the short-term system of truck delivery.'

resident_site_choice.evidence: none of the case communities included community members in decision-making, such as where to develop the relocation site; A greater percentage of NHA respondents, over 80 percent, were told rather than consulted.

tenure_destination.evidence: Table 4: St. Francis 21.0% have a certificate for the house, none for the land; 'less than 1 percent stated they had a certificate for the land their house is on... without certificates for both the house and the land “we are still squatters”'.

hazard_binding.evidence: [para] City officials said some sites were built on floodplains; no site-level hazard screening is described.

funding.evidence: Funding instrument not described at site level.

distance.evidence: each site was further from the city center than we could theoretically justify as even partially in the set of 'close' (calibration: 10 km crossover, >15 km fully out); Suribao 'close to Tacloban City center' score 0.10.

hazard_at_destination.evidence: In December of 2017, a passing tropical storm flooded several relocation sites and pushed dozens out of their homes. Table 5: St. Francis 12.3% house flooding, 39.7% septic overflow during Tropical Storm Urduja.

return_to_origin.evidence: an astounding 70 percent of St. Francis residents reported electrical limitations, and in interviews respondents shared that limited electricity was motivating decisions to abandon the site and return to previous barangays.

livelihoods.evidence: [para] The report says, for Tacloban North as a whole, that 'inadequate access to reliable livelihood is the most critical issue facing Tacloban North'; there is no site-specific finding.

overall.evidence: Table 4 fuzzy scores for Suribao: built livability 0.38, societal 0.20, livability 0.20 (out of all sets). The report also says visits to St. Francis 'were undeniably eerie'.

cases.notes: 'Suribao' is a pseudonym in Palagi & Javernick-Will (2020). Its Table 1 row (NHA, 1000 planned, 300 occupied, 73 surveyed) is the same as 'St. Francis I' in the same team's 2018 CU Boulder survey report (Table 1). Site-level data from that report are used on the basis of this match. I could not access the other two Palagi papers (JME 2020, IJDRR 2019).

year_start.evidence: With international funding (from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA)) and government support, the move took place in 2005

households.evidence: over 100 villagers living in the Lateu settlement

trigger.evidence: The original site had been flooded on several occasions by storm surge and tsunami events and the community sought an alternative site.

lead.evidence: the community sought an alternative site. With international funding (from the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA)) and government support... The project took place under the banner of Capacity Building for the Development of Adaptation Measures in Pacific Island Countries (CBDAMPIC) coordinated by SPREP.

single_owner.evidence: [para] Implemented by SPREP under the CIDA-funded CBDAMPIC project with government support. No single national public body held land, budget and implementation.

resident_site_choice.evidence: the community sought an alternative site; [para] the site was chosen 'based not only on technical calculations, but also on community input and consent'.

tenure_destination.evidence: Land tenure at Lirak not described in accessible sources.

hazard_binding.evidence: moved to 15 metre, higher ground, around 600 metres from the coast; officials stated 'for the next 50 years, the community of Lirak will be safe from floods, tsunamis and storm surges'

funding.evidence: [para] Paid for by a time-limited donor project (CIDA-funded CBDAMPIC, run by SPREP), not a standing national programme.

distance.evidence: to Lirak, 500 metres away and 30 metres above sea level

hazard_at_destination.evidence: [para] No hazard impact at Lirak reported; post-relocation surveys found that adaptive capacity had improved.

livelihoods.evidence: [para] Rainwater tanks (6 x 6,000 L) were supplied; livelihood outcomes are not described.

overall.evidence: post-relocation surveys found that the adaptive capacity of the community had improved because of the move (Warrick, 2011); [para] a 2007 SPREP evaluation found most residents 'had successfully adjusted to their new environment, felt safer from climate threats, and expressed satisfaction with the overall process'.

cases.notes: Primary sources (Warrick 2011; SPREP post-relocation survey) returned 403 / DNS errors. Distance and elevation differ between sources: 500 m / 30 m (Campbell) vs 600 m / 15 m (Mongabay). A search snippet gave 'about 50 people from 10 households', but I could not verify it, so it is not used.

UCL returns 403 for the Lavell et al. (2015) diagnostic report. The only Wayback snapshot is cut off at 1 MB. The project's closing report (retrieved via Wayback) lists the Yucatán cases as Celestún (Barrio FONDEN, El Arenal-Las Charcas), Progreso (Campestre Flamboyanes) and Tzucacab (El Escondido, Tigre Grande). It has no 'Mérida (South)' case. Searches found no other documentation. Every variable is unknown.

cases.place_destination: El Alto (Cristal I, Cristal II, Palermo)

year_start.evidence: Cristal I constituye el principal barrio de reubicación definitiva de los damnificados. Ha acogido a 68 familias damnificadas por la granizada del 19 de febrero de 2002

households.code: 156 families (68 Cristal I + 73 Cristal II + 15 Palermo)
households.evidence: Ha acogido a 68 familias damnificadas por la granizada del 19 de febrero de 2002; el barrio [Cristal II] ha acogido a 73 familias beneficiarias de la reubicación; 15 familias damnificadas por la granizada del 19 de febrero de 2002 fueron reubicadas allí [Palermo].

trigger.evidence: inundaciones y los deslizamientos de terreno que se presentaron junto con la granizada del 19 de febrero de 2002 dañaron fuertemente las estructuras, y la vivienda, muy en particular.

lead.evidence: Las parcelas construidas que todavía estaban disponibles fueron compradas a 3 000 $ US por el ministerio de Vivienda; [the ministry] procedió, con los organismos financieros, a una licitación ante constructores privados para comprar parcelas construidas.

single_owner.evidence: [para] The Ministry of Housing bought the built plots in El Alto. The La Paz municipality took ownership of the destroyed properties through a title exchange ('un intercambio de actas de propiedad a través del cual la municipalidad de La Paz obtenía la propiedad destruida').

resident_site_choice.evidence: La repartición de los damnificados en los barrios no respondió a ninguna lógica socio-espacial sino simplemente a la cronología.

tenure_destination.evidence: un intercambio de actas de propiedad a través del cual la municipalidad de La Paz obtenía la propiedad destruida [in exchange for the new house]

hazard_binding.evidence: No hazard assessment of the El Alto sites is described.

funding.evidence: [para] The Ministry of Housing bought the plots at US$3,000 each with 'organismos financieros'; the source does not say whether this came from a standing programme or emergency funds.

distance.evidence: aproximadamente a una hora y media en bus desde el centro de La Paz

hazard_at_destination.evidence: No hazards at Cristal I, II or Palermo are reported.

return_to_origin.evidence: la mayoría ha decidido regresar a vivir al municipio de La Paz; otros damnificados abandonaron completamente los barrios de reubicación

livelihoods.evidence: [para] Transport costs amount to 'entre el tercio y la mitad de los ingresos de un adulto activo'; brick-makers kept production in hazardous Llojeta.

overall.evidence: [para] The authors conclude that relocation ignored 'condiciones socioeconómicas ni las aspiraciones de las personas'. Many returned, accepting 'una mayor exposición a la amenaza' to keep access to La Paz and its services.

cases.notes: Hardy & Combaz (2009). Cristal II may also include victims of the 2003 Alto Llojeta landslide; the case is coded on the 2002 hailstorm relocation. The distance code rests on 1.5 h by bus from central La Paz; the source gives no km figure.

year_start.evidence: [para] CU survey report Table 2: UNDP site (= Ulot) 100% of respondents moved in 2017.

households.evidence: Ulot NGO 55 55 40 (planned occupancy, validated occupancy, sample size)

trigger.evidence: Following Typhoon Haiyan, the city government decided to relocate informal settlers (up to 40 percent of the city's population) to the largely undeveloped northern edges of the city

lead.evidence: Ulot is listed as an NGO project (non-NHA); the matching CU report site is 'UNDP NGO 40 55 55 100'.

single_owner.evidence: [para] Non-government developer on land coordinated by the city; utilities such as water came from the city ('none of the sites are connected to the municipal water system').

resident_site_choice.evidence: Notably, none of the case communities included community members in decision-making, such as where to develop the relocation site.

tenure_destination.evidence: Table 4: UNDP 12.1% certificate for the house, none for the land; less than 1 percent stated they had a certificate for the land their house is on.

distance.evidence: each site was further from the city center than we could theoretically justify as even partially in the set of 'close' (10 km crossover); Ulot 'close to Tacloban City center' score 0.19.

hazard_at_destination.evidence: Table 5 (Tropical Storm Urduja): UNDP house flooding '-', house damage '-', septic overflow '-'.

return_to_origin.evidence: Validated occupancy 55 of 55; no returns reported.

overall.evidence: Table 4 fuzzy scores for Ulot: built livability 0.14, societal livability 0.57, livability 0.14. The CU report adds '90 percent of respondents at UNDP reported no construction defects' and notes 42 percent had monthly road-access limits.

cases.notes: 'Ulot' is a pseudonym. Its Table 1 row (NGO, 55/55, 40 surveyed) is the same as the 'UNDP' site in the 2018 CU Boulder report. Palagi: residents moved en masse from their sending barangay into a dedicated transitional site and later cohesively into the relocation site. Participation score 0.6 (highest of the 13 sites) but consultative only.

year_start.evidence: [para] Settlement established after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami; year not given.

households.evidence: Table 1: Matara, Southern Province - Labeemwatta - 4 [km to nearest town] - 4-6 [km from original village] - Sinhalese - 99 [households]

trigger.evidence: the authorities declared a buffer zone along the coast to prevent the affected families from setting down again near the coast. Many new settlements were built away from the coast

lead.evidence: [para] Resettlement was supported by 'a whole range of agencies, both local and foreign'; the agency for this site is not named.

tenure_destination.evidence: Land-rights scores are in Appendix B, which is an image and could not be extracted.

distance.evidence: Distance from original village (km): 4-6 (the range crosses the 5 km threshold)

return_to_origin.evidence: [para] The paper notes in general that many resettled families returned to the coast; there is no site-specific data.

livelihoods.evidence: Site-level scores in Appendix B (image) not extractable.

overall.evidence: [para] 'communities in southern Sri Lanka have performed better on a majority of indicators'; the three below-average communities are all in the East. The score for Labeemwatta itself is only in a figure.

cases.notes: Hettige et al. (2018). Per-community recovery scores (Fig. 2, Appendix B) are images and could not be read. Because the paper puts all three below-average (<2.5) sites in the East, this Southern site was probably at or above average, but that is not coded. Searches found no other documentation.

year_start.evidence: 80% of households decided to relocate from their old village 'Mondo' to their new home 'Keigold' after an earthquake in 2007, as part of a self-initiative.

households.evidence: 80% of households decided to relocate from their old village 'Mondo' to their new home 'Keigold'

trigger.evidence: [para] The community lived in seaside Mondo on Ranongga and moved to the hills after the 2007 earthquake caused a landslide that made the village unsafe.

lead.evidence: as part of a self-initiative; [para] the relocation is described as a case of pro-active community transformation.

single_owner.evidence: Government role not described in accessible sources.

resident_site_choice.evidence: [para] Self-initiated relocation: households decided to move to Keigold.

distance.evidence: [para] Keigold is in the hills above the coast (about 145 m above sea level); no distance given.

return_to_origin.evidence: [para] About 20% of households did not relocate; returns are not described.

overall.evidence: The reallocation process can be seen as a case of pro-active community transformation that provides valuable lessons to other rural communities

cases.notes: The full text of Ha'apio et al. (2018) and the RNZ article returned 403. Coding uses abstract text surfaced in search results and the RNZ snippet. The hazard in the sample frame is 'other': an earthquake-triggered landslide. Government support is not documented.

year_start.evidence: Beneficiaries began moving into the sites covered by this pathway, Gamay, Hitunlob, and Sambawan, within a year and a half of Typhoon Haiyan.

trigger.evidence: Following Typhoon Haiyan, the city government decided to relocate informal settlers (up to 40 percent of the city's population) to the largely undeveloped northern edges of the city

lead.evidence: The first pathway covered three non-governmental communities, Gamay, Hitunlob, and Sambawan. One was managed by the local-office of an international organization while the other two were funded by social responsibility foundations of national corporations.

single_owner.evidence: two different organizations formed a similar team for Sambawan... None secured the city's required development permit before transferring households... necessitating the follow-on of requisite infrastructure services by other NGOs or the government.

resident_site_choice.evidence: Notably, none of the case communities included community members in decision-making, such as where to develop the relocation site.

tenure_destination.evidence: Table 4: SM Cares 9.9% certificate for the house, none for the land, 4.9% informed of a future payment plan; less than 1 percent overall had a land certificate.

funding.evidence: [para] Funded by a corporate social-responsibility foundation; the codebook categories do not clearly apply.

distance.evidence: each site was further from the city center than we could theoretically justify as even partially in the set of 'close' (10 km crossover); Sambawan 'close to Tacloban City center' score 0.03, but near the Tacloban North local hub (score 0.88; <3 km).

hazard_at_destination.evidence: Table 5 (Tropical Storm Urduja, Dec 2017): SM Cares 5.8% house flooding, 20.9% septic overflow; 'a passing tropical storm flooded several relocation sites'.

livelihoods.evidence: “Of course, the poverty here, because the livelihood really is far. For me, because I found a place to have my livelihood, it's okay; but for other people, I'm sure they are not okay.” (Resident of SM Cares; 2016)

overall.evidence: Only five of the thirteen case communities were identified as in the set for both built and societal livability... The remainder of the livable communities were non-governmental: Gamay, Hitunlob, and Sambawan. (Sambawan livability score 0.51.)

cases.notes: 'Sambawan' is a pseudonym. Its Table 1 row (NGO, 600 planned, 495 occupied, 86 surveyed) is the same as 'SM Cares' in the 2018 CU Boulder report. The livability score (0.51) is only just in the set, so the 'success' code is relative to the other Tacloban sites.

year_start.evidence: The relocation position of the Sijeruk landslide victims in 2004, experienced a landslide again in 2008

trigger.evidence: The relocation site of the Sijeruk-Banjarnegara landslide victims had experienced a landslide again

hazard_binding.evidence: That means the location selection for relocation was not safe from the landslide. Land suitability analysis for relocation locations was not appropriate.

hazard_at_destination.evidence: The relocation position of the Sijeruk landslide victims in 2004, experienced a landslide again in 2008... it turns out that the relocation point was in a zone prone to landslides.

overall.evidence: One example of a failed relocation was the location of the victims of the Sijeruk landslide, Banjarnegara.

cases.notes: Hidayat (2020) mentions the case only briefly. The source dates the relocation to 2004. The Sijeruk landslide is widely reported as January 2006, so year_start is low confidence.

year_start.evidence: [para] Settlement established after the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami; year not given.

households.evidence: Table 1: Loardstar village - 7 [km to nearest town] - 7-13 [km from original village] - Sinhalese - 56 [households]

trigger.evidence: the authorities declared a buffer zone along the coast to prevent the affected families from setting down again near the coast. Many new settlements were built away from the coast

lead.evidence: [para] Resettlement was supported by 'a whole range of agencies, both local and foreign'; the agency for this site is not named.

return_to_origin.evidence: [para] General statement that many resettled families returned to the coast; no site-specific data.

overall.evidence: [para] Southern communities performed better on a majority of indicators; the site-specific score is only in a figure.

cases.notes: Hettige et al. (2018); same limitations as sample 56. A search result mentions a 'Solideal Loadstar Rehabilitation Trust' camp near Weligama, Matara, but I did not confirm it is the same settlement, so it is not used.

year_start.evidence: [para] By December 2005 the Ma Amritanandamayi trust had adopted and relocated the entire Samanthanpettai village after the tsunami (IPS, Dec 2005).

households.evidence: [one family], along with 340 others, were the beneficiaries of the decision taken by a trust run by the internationally-known spiritual leader Ma Amritanandamayi to adopt and relocate the entire Samanthanpettai village; 375 identical houses laid out in neat rows

trigger.evidence: a trust run by... Ma Amritanandamayi to adopt and relocate the entire Samanthanpettai village [after the 2004 tsunami]

lead.evidence: the decision taken by a trust run by the internationally-known spiritual leader Ma Amritanandamayi to adopt and relocate the entire Samanthanpettai village

single_owner.evidence: [para] A private religious trust adopted the village and built the houses; no public body ran it end to end.

funding.evidence: [para] Charitable trust funds; the codebook categories do not clearly apply.

distance.evidence: [para] Sample frame (from Bavinck et al. 2015) gives a relocation distance of 0.3 km.

livelihoods.evidence: 200 mechanised, fibreglass fishing boats in the village, all of them gifted free by various trusts, compared to the ninety-odd boats this village had before the disaster; 'Life is far better for us now than before the tsunami struck'

overall.evidence: The only accessible assessment is an early (2005) news report; Bavinck et al.'s site-level judgement could not be accessed.

cases.notes: The Bavinck et al. (2015) full text was not accessible. IPS (2005) says a separate cluster of 120 houses was built at Pandangasali for Dalits, 'who had to be clearly segregated from the main group at Samanthanpettai'. The livelihood code reflects only one year after the tsunami.

year_start.evidence: [para] Relocation project launched after the 3-4 February 2010 floods and landslides; houses officially delivered in 2012 ('En agosto de 2012, cinco meses después de la entrega oficial de las viviendas por parte del presidente Felipe Calderón').

households.evidence: es una reubicación parcial en tanto que se realizó para que 462 familias y/o personas se relocalizaran en el nuevo desarrollo habitacional denominado Barrio Sustentable Monarca.

trigger.evidence: Barrio Sustentable Monarca, el cual tuvo el objetivo de brindarles casas seguras fuera de la zona de inundación y deslizamiento [after the 2010 disaster]

lead.evidence: De los 34 entrevistados, 26 personas tuvieron un nivel nulo de participación, mientras que las ocho restantes mantuvieron un nivel de participción bajo, y no hubo persona que manifestara haber sido consultada para que diera su opinión sobre algún aspecto de la reubicación o haber sido partícipe en la toma de decisiones.

single_owner.evidence: [para] Federal (Sedesol), state (Instituto de Vivienda del Estado de Michoacán) and municipal bodies were involved, with FONDEN funding.

resident_site_choice.evidence: no hubo persona que manifestara haber sido consultada para que diera su opinión sobre algún aspecto de la reubicación; Las autoridades señalaron que las dos primeras propuestas fueron rechazadas...

tenure_destination.evidence: No statement on deeds or ownership found.

hazard_binding.evidence: Las autoridades señalaron que las dos primeras propuestas fueron rechazadas por la lejanía del pueblo y por la susceptibilidad de los predios a inundarse... Se hace énfasis en que una vez que se eligió el sitio se solicitaron los estudios de factibilidad y de riesgos, a pesar de que primero debieron elaborarse éstos para posteriormente realizar la elección y compra del terreno.

funding.evidence: En total la erogación proveniente del Fondo de Desastres Naturales (Fonden) para la atención a la emergencia y las obras de reconstrucción fue de $1 274 875 205, y se invirtieron $112 000 000 para la construcción del Barrio Sustentable Monarca.

distance.evidence: El tercer predio denominado Las Mesas, elegido para la construcción de las casas, tiene una superficie de 26 hectáreas y se ubica a 0.8 km del centro de población.

hazard_at_destination.evidence: [Specialists from UMSNH and UNAM warned the site has] un gran deslizamiento conformado por depósitos aluviales y coluviales, además de que el terreno ha sido afectado por numerosos escurrimientos superficiales y subsuperficiales.

return_to_origin.evidence: En agosto de 2012... hubo una ocupación aproximada del 30% de las casas construidas. Para el 2015 la ocupación habitacional continuó manteniéndose por debajo del 50 por ciento. (Returns as such are not described.)

livelihoods.evidence: [para] Relocation restricted animal-raising, kitchen gardens and firewood collection, added transport costs to work, and residents lost food security and alternative income.

overall.evidence: hasta el momento en Angangueo el objetivo de la reubicación no se ha cumplido

cases.notes: Rodríguez García et al. (2016). FONDEN is coded standing_programme because it is Mexico's permanent disaster fund. Occupancy stayed below 50% through 2015, but the source does not say whether non-occupants stayed in or returned to hazard zones.

year_start.evidence: [para] Residents voted in 1992 to initiate the relocation process. No physical relocation has taken place.

households.evidence: As of 2018, Kivalina was home to 440 residents living in approximately 70 homes.

trigger.evidence: [para] Relocation sought because of storm surges, sea-ice changes and coastal erosion threatening the village.

lead.evidence: Residents voted to move to Igrugaivik in 1998 and Kiniktuuraq in 2000, both of which were rejected by the USACE.

single_owner.evidence: In the absence of a lead entity, federal agencies individually prioritize assistance to villages on the basis of their programs' criteria.

resident_site_choice.evidence: Residents voted to move to Igrugaivik in 1998 and Kiniktuuraq in 2000, both of which were rejected by the USACE.

hazard_binding.evidence: [para] The USACE 2006 Master Plan found Kiniktuuraq did not merit further consideration because of coastal erosion, flooding and ice-rich permafrost; community-voted sites were 'rejected by the USACE'.

funding.evidence: [para] No dedicated relocation programme; the village 'continues to apply for state and federal funding and support'.

distance.evidence: [para] Destination unresolved; Kiniktuuraq was described as a coastal site about a mile south, but it was rejected.

overall.evidence: Kivalina, Shaktoolik, and Shishmaref... have yet to identify sites that federal, state, and village officials agree are safe, sustainable, and desirable.

cases.notes: The relocation never happened; the literature calls it a 'motionless relocation' (Durrer 2011). 'Failure' here means the relocation process failed, not a failed move. The USACE rejection details come from a search summary of the 2006 Master Plan. I did not open the Master Plan PDF directly.

year_start.evidence: [para] The Nation held community discussions, forums and a tribal-membership vote before deciding to relocate in 2011. 'The development of the Relocation Master Plan began in spring 2014.'

trigger.evidence: [para] The lower village faces tsunami risk and flooding from sea-level rise; the upland area 'is well above the tsunami and flood zones'.

lead.evidence: [para] The Quinault Indian Nation decided after community forums and a membership vote, and engagement included 'specific outreach to different community groups, community surveys, and collaborative design workshops'.

single_owner.evidence: [para] The Nation leads planning and development on its own land, but money comes from many separate federal grants: 'different federal funding sources cannot be combined with one another'.

resident_site_choice.evidence: community surveys, and collaborative design workshops (the upland site was set in the Nation's master plan)

tenure_destination.evidence: [para] The new development site is on tribal land, about a mile uphill from the lower village.

hazard_binding.evidence: approximately 200 acres in size and is well above the tsunami and flood zones

funding.evidence: [para] Federal grants (Administration for Native Americans, DOE, COVID relief), state funds, and the tribe's own timber and casino revenue. The tribe 'requires hundreds of millions more' for homes.

distance.evidence: a half-mile upland from the existing village

hazard_at_destination.evidence: The Generations Building was completed in 2021; no hazard impacts at the upland site reported.

return_to_origin.evidence: [para] As of Feb 2024 no homes had been built in the upland; only infrastructure was complete.

overall.evidence: [para] Ongoing: nine acres of upland infrastructure completed Dec 2023; home construction awaits funding.

cases.notes: Tribally led, pre-emptive and still in progress. The Generations Building (senior and children centre) opened in 2021. The WUNC article quotes the president saying 'We've had to do a lot of convincing'. Distance: half a mile (WA Coastal Network) vs about a mile (WUNC); both are under 5 km.
